title: Install plugin
summary: Find fman++ plugins on GitHub and install one from the palette, without a restart.
html:
Install plugin finds third-party plugins on GitHub, GitLab, Forgejo and in the fman++ catalog, downloads one, unpacks it into your data directory and loads it without a restart.

Running it

Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run Install plugin. There is no default key binding, and the command works regardless of which pane has focus.

It also takes an optional github_repo parameter of the form owner/name. Passing it skips the picker and installs that repo directly — this is how fman++'s own "you pressed a key that does nothing" dialog offers you mherrmann/ArrowNavigation and mherrmann/SwitchPanesWithArrowKeys.

What happens

  1. Discover — fman++ searches GitHub for non-archived repositories tagged with both fman and plugin, GitLab and Forgejo hosts, and the fman++ catalog. Results are cached for the rest of the fman++ session.
  2. Pick — results from the different sources appear together in a quicksearch picker. GitHub results show a description and star count; GitLab and Forgejo results show their host and star count; catalog results show their description and source. Plugins already installed are filtered out.
  3. Review — when you pick a repository, fman++ shows its optional description.md in a review screen. If the file is missing or unavailable, the screen says no description is available. Back returns to the picker with your search text; Install continues.
  4. Resolve a version — fman++ asks for the repo's latest release tag. If the repo has never published a release, it falls back to the newest commit on the default branch. So an unreleased plugin still installs; it is just pinned to a commit.
  5. Download and unpack into %APPDATA%\fman\Plugins\Third-party\<repo name>. Catalog ZIP files are checked against their SHA-256 value before installing.
  6. Load it in place, at its correct position in the load order, and show Plugin 'X' was successfully installed.

The steps that block show a status message while they run — Fetching available plugins…, Downloading X….

The order of the list

The picker lists most recently pushed first, with the most-starred first among equally recent ones. Stars break ties only: a 900-star plugin last touched in 2019 still ranks below a one-star plugin pushed this morning.

That is deliberately not GitHub's own relevance order — for a query that is nothing but two topics, relevance is near-uniform and the resulting order is effectively arbitrary. It is also not GitHub's "recently updated", which any metadata change bumps: renaming a repo or editing its description would float an abandoned plugin to the top.

A repo that has never been pushed to sorts to the bottom, where the star count decides the order.

Rate limits and privacy

  • fman++ talks to the public GitHub API anonymously — no token, no sign-in. Anonymous calls are limited to 60 requests an hour per IP, and search to 10 a minute. A normal install is three or four requests, so on a shared or NAT'd address you may still hit the limit.
  • fman++ sends no identifying data with these requests. GitHub sees your IP and the default user agent, and nothing in the URL but the query.
  • Nothing is contacted until you run the command. fman++ does not poll GitHub in the background, and there is no update check for installed plugins.

Updating a plugin

There is no Update plugin command. Updating means Remove plugin, then Install plugin again.

After an install, fman++ records the repo and the installed version in the plugin's Plugin.json:

{ "url": "https://api.github.com/repos/mherrmann/ArrowNavigation", "ref": "v1.0.2" }

ref is a release tag, or a commit SHA when the plugin had no release. List plugins reads it back and shows it beside each third-party plugin, abbreviating a SHA to its first 8 characters.

When it goes wrong

Symptom Cause
Could not fetch available plugins: <reason>. Network, DNS or TLS failure during the search.
Nothing in the picker No eligible repo carries both the fman and plugin topics, or you already have all of them.
Plugin X seems to already be installed. The destination directory exists. Remove it first — nothing is ever overwritten.
HTTP 403 GitHub rate limit. Wait, or install by owner/name to spend fewer requests.

If loading fails after the download, no success alert appears — but the files are already on disk, so remove the directory, or use Remove plugin, before retrying.

When signed in to a fman++ account, successful installs update that account's shared plugin list, and Remove plugin removes the entry. Local plugins without saved source details are not uploaded. See Syncing plugins between computers for account sync details.

Installing without GitHub

Nothing about fman++'s plugin loader requires GitHub. Copy a plugin directory into %APPDATA%\fman\Plugins\User\ and run Reload plugins.

On macOS and Linux that path is ~/Library/Application Support/fman/Plugins/User and ~/.config/fman/Plugins/User; setting FMAN_DATA_DIRECTORY moves it anywhere.

title: Status bar
summary: The one-line strip along the bottom — what it tells you, and how to switch it off.
html:
The status bar is the strip along the bottom of fman++'s window. It shows the latest message from fman++ or a plugin, and can also show a selection summary, an Incognito marker, and controls for minimized progress dialogs.

What it shows

There is a single message slot, left-aligned. Whatever wrote last wins.

When Message
Startup v1.7.8 ready. — or Updated to v1.7.8. Changelog after a version change, where Changelog is a clickable link
Copy or cut to the clipboard Copying foo.txt, Cutting foo.txt and 3 other files, Copied C:\dir\foo.txt to the clipboard
Reloading plugins Reloaded 2 plugins.
Saving in the text viewer Saved, Saved as <path>, Could not save: <reason>
Auto-reload and tail toggles Auto-reload on, Tail mode on, Auto-reload off, File changed on disk (not reloaded)
Any other viewer action Reloaded from disk, Edit mode, Font size 12, Zoom 125%, Paused, the name of the file Next or Previous landed on
Viewer navigation Advance only for same type: on, No further file to view
Long-running work a "doing X…" line for as long as the work runs, then cleared
Nothing recent Ready.

Messages either sit there until something replaces them, or carry a timeout after which the bar falls back to Ready. — 2 to 5 seconds for the routine ones, longer for hints. A message may contain links; they open in your browser.

Selection summary

When a pane has selected files or folders, the summary can show a count and total size, such as 3 files, 2 folders selected, 12.4 MB. By default, sizes include files but not folder contents. Run Toggle selection summary location to show it in each pane, in the window bar for the focused pane, or in both. Run Toggle selection folder sizes to include folder contents in a background calculation; the default is off. Both commands are in the palette and have no default shortcut.

Incognito and minimized progress dialogs

While Incognito mode is on, a permanent Incognito marker appears at the right of the bar. Toggle the mode to stop recording Go To visits; restarting turns it off. See Incognito mode.

Each minimized progress dialog adds an icon beside the marker. Hover to see the task title and click to restore it. Resume tool window restores the only minimized dialog directly or lets you choose when there are several; Minimize tool window minimizes the most recently shown eligible dialog.

Turning it off

Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run Toggle status bar. The bar disappears immediately and the panes grow into the row it occupied — the window keeps its size on screen. Running the command again brings it back, and the choice survives a restart.

Command name Palette label Platform Default key
toggle_status_bar Toggle status bar all none (palette only)
toggle_incognito Toggle incognito mode all none (palette only)
toggle_pane_status_lines Toggle pane status lines all none (palette only)
toggle_pane_messages_in_status_bar Toggle pane messages in status bar all none (palette only)
resume_tool_window Resume tool window all none (palette only)
minimize_tool_window Minimize tool window all none (palette only)

statusbar, hide status bar, message bar, bottom bar and chrome also find the row. They are hidden keywords, so it still reads Toggle status bar.

{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+S"], "command": "toggle_status_bar" }

Notes

  • Messages are not lost, just not drawn. fman++ and plugins keep posting them while the bar is hidden, and the latest one is there when you bring the bar back. Nothing errors, nothing queues up.
  • Hiding it is not the same as hiding the title bar. The status bar is an ordinary part of the window, so switching it off has none of the frameless-window caveats — the window stays draggable and closable.
  • The state survives a restart without a flash, applied before the window is first shown.
  • The state is saved as status_bar_visible in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json. The key is only written while the bar is hidden; a visible bar is the absence of the key.

Theming

A theme paints the bar through two tokens:

Token What it paints
statusbar_bg_top Top of the vertical background gradient
statusbar_bg_bottom Bottom of it — falls back to statusbar_bg_top, so naming only the one token gives a flat bar

The text colour is bright_fg and the line above the bar is border; both are shared with the rest of the chrome. The font size is set in Theme.css under the .statusbar selector — 8pt by default, 11pt on macOS.

Pane status lines

Each pane can show a short-lived message line below its file list or viewer. The line is hidden when empty, and each pane keeps its own message. By default, pane messages appear both there and in the window-wide status bar. Run Toggle pane status lines to show or hide the lines, and Toggle pane messages in status bar to control whether those messages also appear in the window bar. Both settings persist across restarts and the commands have no default shortcut. If pane lines are hidden, pane messages go to the window bar.

The pane line shares the status bar's theme by default; themes can customize its background, text, and border independently.

title: The tutorial
summary: The speech bubble that teaches GoTo, the command palette and the two panes — and how to run it again.
html:
The tutorial is fman++'s onboarding tour: a small speech bubble that walks you through GoTo, the command palette and the two panes.

It starts by itself on the first run, in the left pane. Afterwards you can start it again from the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P → Tutorial), and on macOS from the Help menu. If you abort the tour on a first run and then reach for the mouse, fman++ offers it once more.

A second tour, Cleanup guide, uses the same bubble to walk you through tidying a folder.

Where the bubble sits

Bottom right of the window, with a small margin, above the status bar when that is shown. The position is deliberately stable: the bubble does not follow the cursor, the active pane, or a dialog.

It moves in exactly one case — when an open dialog would overlap it, it hops to just above that dialog, still right-aligned.

Driving it from the keyboard

The tour is meant to teach the keyboard, so it can be driven from the keyboard.

  • Enter activates the focused button, which is painted as the default one so you can see where Enter would go.
  • Arrow keys move between the buttons — Left and Up back, Right and Down forward, wrapping around.
  • Alt and the underlined letter activates a button wherever focus is.
  • The last button is the affirmative one by convention, and it is the one focused when a step opens.

Where the keyboard goes

Each step decides for itself whether the bubble takes focus:

The step asks you to… Keyboard goes to
Press a key in the pane — "press Tab", "press F5", "type its name" the directory pane
Acknowledge and move on — "Yes"/"No", "Continue", "Close" the bubble's buttons

While a bubble holds the keyboard, fman++'s own shortcuts do not fire and the pane's cursor row loses its highlight. Both come back when the step closes and focus is handed back to the pane, so the next step's instructions land where you expect.

title: Go to
summary: Jump a pane anywhere by typing a few letters, plus named commands for the folders that are awkward to type.
html:
GoTo jumps a pane to another directory without walking the tree. It is a fuzzy-search prompt on Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS), and a set of palette commands cover the places that are awkward to type — your home directory, Desktop, AppData, %TEMP%.

Usage

  1. Press Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS).
  2. Start typing. The list filters as you go: directories whose path starts with what you typed rank first, then ones whose name does, then substring matches, then loose character matches. Type home for your home directory, desktop for the Desktop. Type > first to switch to the Command Palette.
  3. Press Tab to complete the highlighted entry and keep typing below it.
  4. Press Enter, or click, to open it in the active pane.

Where the suggestions come from

Suggestions are the directories you have already visited, ranked by how often — fman++ counts every path change in Visited Paths.json. Your home directory, Desktop, Documents and Downloads are always in the list too, even if you have never opened them in fman++.

From three characters on, fman++ also asks the OS search index — Windows Search, Spotlight on macOS — for up to ten more folders whose name starts with your query, so a directory you have never opened in fman++ can still show up.

If a directory you pick has since been deleted, fman++ drops it from the history instead of showing an error, so it stops being suggested.

Incognito mode

Run Toggle incognito mode from the command palette to stop adding Go To visits to history. Existing suggestions and saved history remain available. When you quit, fman++ keeps the pane folders saved before you enabled the mode. Turning it off returns each pane to its earlier folder and file; a deleted folder resolves to its nearest existing parent. Window size, position and version are still saved. Incognito mode turns off after restarting fman++. The status bar shows a permanent Incognito marker while it is on.

Typing paths

Command name Palette label Default key

  • The everyday four are offered, but not promoted.   • They match on their name, not just their path. Each shows a name on the right of the row — Home, Desktop, Documents, Downloads — and typing it finds the row even when the path shares no letters with it. That is what makes home reach ~. title: Rename
summary: Rename inline in the file list, with a Retry that keeps the name you typed when the file is locked.
html:
Rename renames the file or folder under the cursor by editing its name in place in the file list — no dialog. A failed rename offers Retry, so the name you typed is never thrown away just because another program had the file open.

For moving a file somewhere else, or renaming and moving in one step, use Move (F6). Rename deliberately refuses paths.

Usage

  1. Put the cursor on a file or folder.
  2. Press F2 or Shift+F6 — or run Rename from the command palette, or pick Rename from the file's right-click menu.
  3. The name becomes an editable field in place, with part of it preselected.
  4. Type the new name and press Enter. Esc cancels.

After a successful rename the cursor follows the item to its new name.

Commands

Command name Palette label Default key Shown when
rename Rename F2, Shift+F6 something is under the cursor

It is also in the right-click menu of any item, file or folder. It is deliberately absent from the menu you get on empty space in a pane, where there is nothing to rename.

What gets preselected

  • For a file, everything up to the extension, so typing replaces the base name and keeps .txt. The double extensions .tar.gz, .tar.xz and .pkg.tar.xz count as one extension.
  • For a folder, the whole name — folders have no extension to protect.

When it refuses

  • A name containing a path separator, or .. or ., is refused with "Relative paths are not supported. Please use Move (F6) instead." On Windows both \ and / count.
  • A name that already exists is refused with "<name> already exists!" — rename never silently overwrites. Move is the command that asks about overwriting.
  • An empty or unchanged name does nothing at all, silently.

Case-only renames do work: Foo to foo is not treated as "already exists", even on a case-insensitive filesystem.

Retry on failure

If the rename fails, the alert offers Retry (the default, so Enter retries) and Cancel:

Access was denied trying to rename pdf-to-jpg to _old_pdf-to-jpg.
                    [ Retry ]  [ Cancel ]

Retry re-attempts the same rename with the same target name. The usual cause is another program holding the file or folder open — an editor, a terminal sitting in that directory, a git GUI. Close it, press Enter, done. Cancel and Esc both give up.

A permission failure produces the "Access was denied" wording above; any other failure says "Could not rename X to Y." Both offer Retry.

In a folder that needs administrator rights (C:\Program Files\…) the rename raises a UAC prompt instead — Retry could never succeed there. See Administrator rights for protected folders.

Notes

  • Usually instant. The new name always lands in the same directory, so on a local filesystem the progress dialog never gets a chance to appear.
  • Inside an archive it is real work. 7-Zip rewrites the archive, with a progress bar and a working Cancel.

title: Select theme
summary: Switch fman++'s colors from the command palette, applied immediately and remembered.
html:
Select theme switches fman++'s color theme from the command palette and applies it immediately — no restart.

Usage

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run Select theme.
  2. A quicksearch list shows every installed theme. The active one is preselected and marked current. Type to fuzzy-filter, like any other palette list.
  3. Pick one with Enter or a click. The panes, header, status bar, location bar, dialogs and the palette itself recolor right away, and the choice is remembered across restarts.

Bundled themes

Monokai (default), Dark, Light, Solarized Dark, Solarized Light, Nord, Dracula, Gruvbox Dark, High Contrast, WezTerm, Matrix, Windows 11 Light and Windows 11 Dark.

Matrix also ships slightly translucent ("opacity": 0.92). Use Set window opacity to override that, or to fade any other theme.

What a theme can change besides colors

  • Icons. A theme may name an icon set and an icon size, so switching theme can change every icon in the panes. Select icon set overrides that, or picks a set without changing your colors.
  • Font. A theme may name a font family too — eight of the thirteen bundled themes do. Select font overrides that, or picks a family without changing your colors.

Commands

Command name Palette label Default key
select_theme Select theme none (palette only)

Change theme, color scheme, colors, dark mode and skin find it too. They are hidden keywords, so the row still reads Select theme.

{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+T"], "command": "select_theme" }

Notes

  • A file viewer that is already open — text, image or video — keeps its old colors until you close and reopen it. Those viewers copy the pane's colors when they open.
  • Context menus on Windows and macOS stay native-looking under every theme.
  • The choice is saved as theme in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json.

title: View file
summary: Open the file under the cursor in fman++'s own viewer instead of an external application.
html:
View file opens fman++'s internal viewer on the file under the cursor, showing its contents inside the active pane instead of launching an external application.

fman++ picks the viewer from the file:

  • Images (.png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .bmp, .webp, .ico, .svg) open the image viewer.
  • Videos (.mp4, .m4v, .mkv, .webm, .avi, .mov, .wmv, .flv, .mpg, .mpeg, .ogv, .3gp, .ts) open the video viewer.
  • Everything else is checked for binary content. Text-like files open the text viewer; a binary such as an .exe or a .zip shows an alert instead of being rendered as garbage.

Usage

  1. Put the cursor on a file.
  2. Open the command palette, search "view" or "internal viewer", and run View file.
  3. The file's contents fill the active pane. Press Escape, Enter or Backspace to close it and return to the file list — or press Ctrl+Shift+P for the viewer's own command palette.

Commands

Command name Palette label Also found by Default key
view_file View file view, internal viewer, preview none (palette only)
view_file_in_other_pane View file in other pane view in other pane none (palette only)

Those extra words are hidden keywords: they find the command without ever being shown. Bind either like any other command:

{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+V"], "command": "view_file" }

Previewing side by side

View file in other pane opens the same viewer for the file under the cursor but mounts it in the other pane, so the current pane's file list stays visible. Keyboard focus deliberately stays where it was, so you can keep moving the cursor through the folder and preview each file as you go.

With only one pane open it falls back to viewing in place, and there the viewer takes focus as usual.

Notes

  • Enter and double-click are unaffected. This is a separate, palette-only path — pressing Enter or double-clicking a file still opens it with the OS default application.
  • Running the command on a directory, or on a path that is not a local file, shows an alert instead of opening the viewer.
  • Running it with nothing under the cursor shows "No file is selected!".
  • Next / previous file inside an open viewer re-runs this command: it steps the pane cursor to the neighbouring file and routes to the matching viewer.

title: Toggle title bar and menu bar
summary: Take the window frame away for a borderless fman++ — and how to get it back once there is nothing left to click.
html:
Two commands turn off window chrome fman++ does not need. Each toggles on its own, applies immediately, and is remembered across restarts.

  • Toggle title bar — the OS title bar around the window. Every platform.
  • Toggle menu bar — fman++'s Help menu. macOS only: that menu is the only one fman++ has, and it lives in the system menu bar at the top of the screen rather than inside fman++'s window. On Windows and Linux fman++ has no menu at all, so the command is not registered and does not appear in the palette.

Usage

  1. Press Ctrl+Shift+P and run Toggle title bar — or, on macOS, Toggle menu bar.
  2. The bar disappears right away. Running the same command again brings it back.

There is no on/off list to pick from: each command flips the bar it names.

Commands

Command name Palette label Platform Default key
toggle_title_bar Toggle title bar all none (palette only)
toggle_menu_bar Toggle menu bar macOS only none (palette only)
toggle_pane_location_bars Toggle pane location bars all none (palette only)

Frameless, borderless, window frame and caption find the first; help menu, hide menu and chrome find the second where it exists. They are hidden keywords, so the rows still read Toggle title bar and Toggle menu bar.

Bind them like any other command:

{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+T"], "command": "toggle_title_bar" },
{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+M"], "command": "toggle_menu_bar" }

Below the panes, Toggle status bar controls the window-wide message strip. Toggle pane status lines shows or hides the short-lived message line under each pane, and Toggle pane messages in status bar controls whether those messages also appear in the window bar. These settings persist across restarts; see Status bar. Toggle pane location bars shows or hides the full folder path above each pane. The path lines are visible by default; pane_location_bars_visible in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json is absent when they are visible and false when they are hidden.

Before you turn the title bar off

A window with no title bar has no close button and cannot be dragged. It is a real frameless window, so the OS draws nothing to grab: no drag, no double-click to maximize, no edge resizing, no snapping to a screen half.

Ctrl+Shift+P → Toggle title bar is the way back, and it is worth binding a key to it before you first turn the bar off. While the bar is gone, Center window still moves the window, as does the OS's own move shortcut (Alt+Space, then M, on Windows).

Hiding the title bar also takes away the topmost row of the window, so on Windows and Linux the palette is then only reachable by its key binding.

Notes

  • The window keeps the screen space it had. Hiding the title bar grows the panes into the row the bar occupied instead of shrinking the window by it; showing it again restores the size the window had before the toggle.
  • The state survives a restart without a flash. Both bars are applied before the window is first shown, so a hidden bar is never briefly visible at startup.
  • Hiding the title bar hides the window title with it. fman++ still sets the two-pane path string, nothing draws it, and it returns unchanged when the bar does.
  • On macOS the menu bar is the system one, at the top of the screen rather than inside fman++'s window. Toggle menu bar hides the Help menu there. Toggle title bar works everywhere.
  • The two bars never sit on top of each other. On macOS the Help menu is in the system bar, not below fman++'s title bar; on Windows and Linux there is no menu.
  • The state is saved as title_bar_visible and menu_bar_visible in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json, beside theme and window_opacity. A key is only written while its bar is hidden — a visible bar is the absence of the key.

title: Window functions
summary: Everything that changes the fman++ window itself — the bars, how see-through it is, and where it sits on screen.
html:
These are the commands that change fman++'s window itself rather than what is inside it: how much of it you see, how solid it is, and where it sits on the screen.

None of them has a default key binding. They are all reached from the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), and all of them except Center window are remembered across restarts.

Command What it does
toggle_title_bar Hides the OS title bar, and the window frame with it
toggle_menu_bar Hides fman++'s Help menu — macOS only
toggle_status_bar Hides the message strip along the bottom

On Windows, Minimize to taskbar keeps fman++ in the taskbar. The optional system-tray behavior and its commands are described in System tray.

The dim behind dialogs is the odd one out: it has no command, because it is not something you switch on. It is a theme color.

The bars around the panes

The title bar, the macOS menu bar and the status bar each toggle on their own, and each stays off across restarts. The pane status commands control the per-pane message lines and whether their messages are copied to the window bar; see Pane status lines. The path line above each pane has its own saved command, Toggle pane location bars.

Two things worth knowing before hiding the title bar:

  • A frameless window cannot be dragged or closed with the mouse. Read the caveats on Toggle title bar and menu bar first.
  • The window keeps the screen space either way: hiding a bar grows the panes into the row it occupied rather than shrinking the window, and showing it again restores the exact previous size.

How solid the window is

Set window opacity offers Theme default, then 100% down to 70%. The whole window fades, text included — fman++ does not do background-only translucency. The command palette, pick lists and text prompts are drawn inside the window and follow its opacity; alerts and progress dialogs stay opaque.

Theme default is the way back to letting the theme decide. It is not the same as 100%, which pins the window opaque under every theme, including one that ships translucent. A theme sets its own value with the opacity key; your choice wins over it and survives a theme switch.

Dimming behind dialogs

While the command palette, another pick list or a text prompt is open, fman++ lays a scrim over the main window. These dialogs are drawn inside the movable, resizable window; clicking the scrim closes them like Esc. Alerts and the file-open dialog remain separate modal windows.

The embedded dialog stays clear above the dimmed file list.

  • It is the scrim_bg color token, and its alpha byte is the strength. #80000000 — the default — is 50% black, #40000000 a quarter, and #00000000 no dim at all.
  • The progress dialog is excluded. A copy can run for minutes, and a window dimmed that long costs more than the contrast is worth.
  • There is no command and no setting: a theme owns it, like any other color.

Center window

Center window puts fman++ back in the middle of the screen it is already on.

  • Centered within the screen's available area, so a taskbar does not push the window off-centre.
  • On multiple monitors it stays on the monitor it was on, rather than jumping to the primary one.
  • Nothing is remembered — it is a one-shot move, not a mode.

center window on screen, move window to center and middle find it too. They are hidden keywords, so the row still reads Center window.

title: Drag to last used app
summary: Drop the selected files into the app you used last, steering the drag with the keyboard.
html:
Drag to last used app sends the selected local files — or the file under the cursor — into another app by drag and drop, without you having to arrange the two windows side by side. Windows only.

How it works

  1. Run Drag to last used app from the command palette. fman++ shows up to five recently used app windows in a searchable list, with each executable name beside it and the drag controls below. Press Enter to choose the highlighted app and begin, or Esc to cancel.
  2. fman++ brings the chosen window to the front and moves the mouse to its centre.
  3. The drag starts right away, at the window's centre:
    • W A S D or the arrow keys move the cursor — hold a key to keep moving.
    • Q, Space or Enter drops the files.
    • Esc cancels.

You can also move the real mouse and click to drop.

title: Robocopy
summary: Copy or move files with Windows' own robocopy, with tunable threads, retries and logs.
html:
Copy or move selected files and folders with Windows' native robocopy.exe. Run Copy with robocopy or Move with robocopy from the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P). Both are Windows-only and hidden on macOS and Linux. Normal F5 / F6 behaviour is unchanged, and there are no default key bindings or context-menu entries.

Usage

  1. Select files or folders in the active pane. With nothing selected, the entry under the cursor is used.
  2. Run Copy with robocopy or Move with robocopy.
  3. The destination prompt opens with the opposite pane's folder filled in and selected, as it does for F5/F6. Press Enter to accept it, or type another absolute drive or UNC folder path.

The destination receives each selected item by name, including empty subfolders. Unselected siblings are left alone.

With the transfer queue off, only one operation runs at a time, including destination selection and cleanup. Starting another reports “A Robocopy operation is already active.” With queueing on, another operation waits in the shared transfer queue and starts when it reaches the head.

Cancel stops the running robocopy.exe; whatever was already copied or moved stays as it is. If fman++ itself crashes during a transfer, robocopy.exe keeps running.

What to expect

  • Robocopy's own rules apply. Exit codes 0–7 mean no reported copy failure; 8 or higher is a failure. That does not prove every selected item was copied or moved.
  • No safety net. There is no staging, rollback, undo or content verification. A canceled or failed operation can leave partial files at the destination and a partially moved selection. Move checks the selected items afterwards and reports what remains.
  • Data, attributes and timestamps are copied.
  • Links are not followed. Selected links and junctions are refused; links nested inside a selected folder are skipped. A junction at the destination can redirect writes, and overwriting a hard-linked destination file changes its other names too.
  • Refused paths: relative paths, wildcards, device paths, alternate data streams, copying an item onto itself, and copying a folder into itself. Use plain absolute local-drive or UNC paths.
  • Robocopy replaces read-only destination files without asking and applies the source attributes. The ask_before_replacing_read_only setting does not apply.
  • The progress display is a busy indicator, with elapsed time and the selected items or current job — not byte progress. Jobs run one after another; robocopy's own multithreading provides the parallelism.
  • A move on the same drive can be faster with F6, because it may rename instead of copying and deleting.

Settings

Put overrides in %APPDATA%\fman\Plugins\User\Settings\Robocopy.json or Robocopy (Windows).json, then run Reload plugins. Unknown keys, wrong types and out-of-range values are rejected.

Setting Default Effect
threads 8 1–32. Robocopy /MT thread count.
retries 1 0–10. Retries per failed operation.
retry_wait_seconds 1 0–30. Wait between retries.
restartable false Use /Z for restartable network transfers.
unbuffered false Use /J, mainly for large files.
log_enabled false Write a transfer log.
open_log_on_finish false Open the log when done. Needs logging on.
log_retention_count 20 1–100. How many logs to keep.

Logs

Logs are off by default. When on, they are written under <DATA_DIRECTORY>\Local\Robocopy\Logs and contain paths, file names, command arguments, robocopy's output, exit codes and the outcome — review a log before sharing it.

title: Check for updates
summary: fman++ tells you when a new release is out, and you can check by hand at any time.
html:
fman++ checks for a newer published release five minutes after its window appears, then every 24 hours while it stays open. When there is one, a dialog names both versions and offers to download and install it. Each release is announced only once. The download has a cancelable progress dialog.

The automatic check stays quiet when you are up to date or the check fails, and does not run in demo mode.

Checking by hand

Run Check for updates from the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P). It always reports the result — up to date, failed, or a new release — and offers to download it even for a release it has announced before. On Windows the downloaded installer runs and fman++ quits; on macOS the downloaded DMG opens while fman++ stays running. Linux opens the GitHub releases page. If a download fails, fman++ shows an alert and opens that page as a fallback.

Automatic updates on Windows

Automatic updates are off by default in installed copies. Run Toggle automatic updates to enable or disable them, and Set automatic update interval to choose a check interval from 1 to 720 hours (default: 24). When an update is ready, a 30-second countdown offers Update now and Cancel. Cancel or Esc postpones it until the next automatic check. Accepting an automatic update closes fman++, installs without the setup wizard and restarts the app. An all-users installation in Program Files needs one UAC confirmation for each automatic update.

These commands also appear in portable copies, but automatic updates only work in an installed Windows version. Manually checking from a portable copy downloads fmanPortable.zip; after confirmation, fman++ replaces its program files while keeping its data, then starts again. A manual Windows update uses the setup wizard when automatic updates are off.

toggle_automatic_updates Toggle automatic updates auto update, automatic update, unattended update none
set_automatic_update_interval Set automatic update interval update interval, update frequency, check frequency none

A stalled connection does not freeze fman++; the window stays responsive.

title: Administrator rights for protected folders
summary: Copy, move, rename, create and delete in Program Files and other protected folders via a UAC prompt.
html:
fman++ runs without administrator rights. When a file operation targets a folder that needs them — C:\Program Files\…, C:\Windows\… — fman++ hands that one operation to Windows, which shows the usual UAC prompt and carries it out. fman++ itself stays unelevated: programs you start from it, drag and drop and network drives all keep working as before.

Windows only, local files only.

Usage

Nothing to learn — use the normal commands. In a protected folder they raise one UAC prompt per operation:

Command In a protected folder
New file (Shift+F4) UAC prompt, file is created, editor opens
New folder (F7) UAC prompt, folder is created
Copy (F5), paste, drag and drop UAC prompt, Windows' own copy dialog
Move (F6), cut and paste UAC prompt, Windows' own move dialog
Rename (F2) UAC prompt
Delete, Delete permanently UAC prompt (after fman++'s own confirmation)

Declining the prompt cancels the operation. New file and New folder then say "You do not have enough permissions to create …"; the others do nothing. For a non-local file system, fman++ does not try a UAC prompt and shows the original creation error instead.

Notes

  • Windows' dialogs, not fman++'s. An elevated copy or move is done by Windows, exactly as in Explorer, so progress, "replace or skip" and folder-merge questions come from Windows for that operation. Everywhere else you still get fman++'s own dialogs.
  • One prompt for the whole selection. Copying 50 files asks once.
  • Moving out counts too. Moving a file out of a protected folder needs rights there, because the original is removed, so it is elevated as well. Copying out is not — reading needs no rights.
  • A destination folder that does not exist yet inside a protected folder is created first, with a UAC prompt of its own — so two prompts. Likewise New folder with a nested name (a\b) asks once per missing level.
  • A single locked file in a normal folder is not covered: the check is per folder. Such a file fails as before — Rename's Retry is the answer there.
  • Saving from an editor is the editor's business. A file opened from a protected folder still cannot be saved unless the editor elevates itself.
  • Not in archives or on network locations.

title: Copy and move
summary: Copy, move and manage file transfers, including conflicts, queues and undo.
html:
Use Copy (F5) and Move (F6) to transfer files between folders. You can also drag files or paste them from the clipboard. On Windows, dragging within the same drive moves files; dragging to another drive or network share copies them. Hold Ctrl to copy or Shift to move. Dropping files out of an archive always copies them.

You can minimize a Copy or Move progress dialog with – and restore it from its status bar icon.

Transfer queue

Transfers use one global queue by default, so each copy or move starts after the one ahead of it finishes. This includes transfers started by dragging or pasting. Run Toggle transfer queue to turn queueing off or on; the setting is queue_transfers in Core Settings.json. A change affects new transfers, while transfers already waiting stay in the queue.

When transfers are waiting, select the status bar icon or run Show transfer queue. The running transfer appears first. You can reorder or remove waiting transfers, but cancel the running one from its progress dialog. A transfer that has to wait briefly shows Transfer queued: …. Delete, Pack, Rename, Symlink and Undo do not use this queue.

Transfer failures

A file that fails during a transfer does not interrupt the operation with a dialog. The app collects the failed names and reasons while it continues with the other files. When everything finishes, one prompt lists the failures and offers to retry them. Files that fail again are offered in another prompt. Errors found while walking a folder tree still use the continue or abort prompt.

Existing destination files

When a destination file already exists, the prompt can show the incoming and existing file sizes and modified dates. On Windows, local .exe and .dll files can also show their program versions. Overwrite is the default. Choose Rename to keep both files and enter a new name, or Rename all to use available numbered names for later conflicts. Folder conflicts merge their contents without a prompt.

On Windows, replacing a read-only file asks for confirmation by default. Choose Yes, Yes to all, No or Abort; No is the default. Run Toggle read-only replace question to turn the prompt off or on. The setting is ask_before_replacing_read_only in Core Settings.json. Replacement uses the incoming file's attributes.

Overwrite details are shown by default. Run Toggle overwrite details or set show_overwrite_details to false in Core Settings.json to hide them.

Canceling a move

For local file-system moves, the app restores completed files to their original locations if you cancel, choose Abort on an overwrite prompt, the folder walk is aborted, or an unexpected error stops the move. A transfer failure does not roll back other files: the failed file stays at its source, and completed moves stay at their destinations. If an original location is no longer free during rollback, the moved file stays at the destination and the app reports the paths it could not restore. A destination file you approved replacing cannot be recovered by this rollback. Plugin file systems and moves run in an elevated process do not use this rollback.

Other options

  • Toggle locked file check checks on Windows whether another program has a file open before a cross-drive move or an overwrite. It is on by default; its setting is check_locked_files in Core Settings.json. Other platforms skip the check.
  • Toggle deselect after copy is on by default. It deselects a copied item after all its transfer tasks succeed. Skipped, failed or unfinished items stay selected. Drag-and-drop, paste and elevated copies leave the selection alone. The setting is deselect_after_transfer in Core Settings.json.
  • Toggle folder tree (Alt+F10) shows a folder-only tree in one pane, with the current folder expanded when it opens. Use Right and Left to expand or collapse, Tab and Shift+Tab to switch panes, Enter to open a folder in the other pane, and Esc to return to the file list. Toggle tree follows cursor makes the other pane follow the selected folder after a short pause; it is off by default and uses tree_follow_cursor in Core Settings.json.
  • For Windows moves across drives and other copy details, see Robocopy.

Run Toggle transfer queue to turn queueing off or on; the setting is queue_transfers in Core Settings.json. A change affects new transfers, while transfers already waiting stay in the queue. When transfers are waiting, select the status bar icon or run Show transfer queue. The running transfer appears first. You can reorder or remove waiting transfers, but cancel the running one from its progress dialog. A transfer that has to wait briefly shows Transfer queued: …. Delete, Pack, Rename, Symlink and Undo do not use this queue. Transfer failures A file that fails during a transfer does not interrupt the operation with a dialog. The app collects the failed names and reasons while it continues with the other files. When everything finishes, one prompt lists the failures and offers to retry them. Files that fail again are offered in another prompt. Errors found while walking a folder tree still use the continue or abort prompt. Existing destination files When a destination file already exists, the prompt can show the incoming and existing file sizes and modified dates. On Windows, local .exe and .dll files can also show their program versions. Overwrite is the default. Choose Rename to keep both files and enter a new name, or Rename all to use available numbered names for later conflicts. Folder conflicts merge their contents without a prompt. On Windows, replacing a read-only file asks for confirmation by default. Choose Yes, Yes to all, No or Abort; No is the default. Run Toggle read-only replace question to turn the prompt off or on. The setting is ask_before_replacing_read_only in Core Settings.json. Replacement uses the incoming file's attributes. Overwrite details are shown by default. Run Toggle overwrite details or set show_overwrite_details to false in Core Settings.json to hide them. Canceling a move For local file-system moves, the app restores completed files to their original locations if you cancel, choose Abort on an overwrite prompt, the folder walk is aborted, or an unexpected error stops the move. A transfer failure does not roll back other files: the failed file stays at its source, and completed moves stay at their destinations. If an original location is no longer free during rollback, the moved file stays at the destination and the app reports the paths it could not restore. A destination file you approved replacing cannot be recovered by this rollback. Plugin file systems and moves run in an elevated process do not use this rollback. Other options Toggle locked file check checks on Windows whether another program has a file open before a cross-drive move or an overwrite. It is on by default; its setting is check_locked_files in Core Settings.json. Other platforms skip the check. Toggle deselect after copy is on by default. It deselects a copied item after all its transfer tasks succeed. Skipped, failed or unfinished items stay selected. Drag-and-drop, paste and elevated copies leave the selection alone. The setting is deselect_after_transfer in Core Settings.json. Toggle folder tree (Alt+F10) shows a folder-only tree in one pane, with the current folder expanded when it opens. Use Right and Left to expand or collapse, Tab and Shift+Tab to switch panes, Enter to open a folder in the other pane, and Esc to return to the file list. Toggle tree follows cursor makes the other pane follow the selected folder after a short pause; it is off by default and uses tree_follow_cursor in Core Settings.json. For Windows moves across drives and other copy details, see Robocopy.

title: Drag selection
summary: Select a range of rows by dragging from the empty part of a file row.
html:
Drag from the empty part of a row to select a range. A click alone does not change the selection. Dragging a file name still starts a file drag to another pane or app.

A plain drag replaces the selection with the rows between the starting row and the pointer. Hold Ctrl (or Cmd on macOS) as you start dragging to add the range to the selection. Move back toward the starting row to shrink the range. At the edge of the list, the view scrolls and extends the selection; in compact view, it scrolls horizontally.

Drag selection is on by default. Run Toggle drag selection to turn it off; dragging from the empty part of a row then drags the file. The choice is saved in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json under drag_selection.

title: Right-button selection
summary: Mark files with the right mouse button while keeping a way to open their context menu.
html:
Right-button selection is off by default, so right-click opens the context menu. Run Toggle right-button selection from the command palette to turn the mode on or off. The choice is saved in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json under right_button_selection.

When the mode is on, right-click a file to mark or unmark it. Drag the right button over rows to apply the starting file's marked state to each row. Hold the right button on a file for one second to open the context menu for the selected files. Right-click empty space and open the menu with the keyboard as usual.

Use the left button on a file name to drag the file to another pane. Drag from the empty part of a row to select a range. Right-button dragging does not scroll the list automatically at its top or bottom edge.

title: Explorer replacement
summary: Open common Windows folders in fman++ and switch back to Explorer when you need it.
html:
On Windows, run Toggle Explorer replacement in the command palette to let an installed copy of fman++ open common folder locations. The setting explorer_replacement in Local/Settings.json is off by default.

When enabled, opening a folder or drive, pressing Win+E, or opening This PC brings up fman++. A folder or drive opens in the active pane if fman++ is already running; This PC opens the drives view. Control Panel, the Recycle Bin and other special folders continue to open in Explorer. The right-click Open action remains Explorer's action. Portable and development builds cannot enable this mode.

Press F10 (Open native file manager) to open Explorer while replacement is enabled. If another program takes over folder opening, fman++ detects it at the next start, turns this setting off and reports the change. You can enable it again from the command palette.

Uninstalling fman++ removes the folder-opening entries it added. If you need to turn the redirect off manually, remove the application subkeys under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Software\\Classes\\Directory\\shell and HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Software\\Classes\\Drive\\shell. If Explorer does not use the restored handlers immediately, sign out and back in.

title: File comments
summary: Add comments to files and folders and see them in the Comment column.
html:
fman++ stores comments in a descript.ion file in the same directory. The format is compatible with Total Commander, so both applications can read and update the same comments.

Add or edit a comment

Select one or more files or folders and press Ctrl+Shift+Z on Windows or Linux, or Cmd+Shift+Z on macOS. If nothing is selected, fman++ edits the item under the cursor. The editor starts with a comment only when all selected items have the same one. Press Enter to save or Shift+Enter to add a line. Saving an empty comment removes it.

Show comments in the file list

The Comment column is included by default. It appears in directories that contain comments and hides automatically in directories without them. It shows the first line of each comment. Use the column header menu or Toggle comment column to show or hide it; a manual choice applies across directories. After copying or moving comments into a directory, the column appears when you next visit or refresh it.

Comments are supported for local files and folders, not archive or FTP locations or network roots. Comments follow items when copied, moved or renamed. Successful trash and permanent deletion remove them; Undo restores comments for trashed items and moves them back with restored files. A read or write problem appears in the status bar and does not change the file operation.

Each directory has one descript.ion file. fman++ preserves entries it does not recognize and keeps an existing file's encoding when possible. New files use UTF-8 with a byte-order mark; when a comment cannot be represented in an existing encoding, fman++ switches the file to that format.

title: File type actions
summary: Choose which app or built-in command opens each kind of file.
html:
Choose what Enter and double-click do for a file type from Open with... → Configure.... Select Always open .md files with... and choose an app, fman++ viewer, fman++ editor (F4) or Command line.... To restore the operating system association, select Stop always opening .md files with ... for that suffix.

File actions are stored in the user data file File Type Actions.json. You can edit it directly:

{
  ".md": {"command_line": ["C:\\Program Files\\Typora\\Typora.exe", "{file}"], "app": "Typora"},
  ".log": {"command": "view_file"},
  ".csv": {"command_line": ["C:\\Tools\\csvview.exe", "--sep", ";", "{file}"]}
}

{file} is replaced with the file path in each argument. If you leave it out, it is added at the end. The longest matching suffix wins, so .tar.gz can have a separate action from .gz. Matching ignores case. Files without an extension have no file type action.

If no action is configured, fman++ uses the system default app. If an action is invalid or cannot run, fman++ shows a status message and falls back to the system default. Run Open with system default to bypass a configured action once.

When you edit an app from Open with → Configure → Edit app, fman++ updates actions that refer to it. Removing an app from the Open with list leaves its saved actions in place. Add app and Edit app ask for arguments after the program name; Enter with only {file} keeps a plain app entry. Apps.json stores each app's command line. A standalone {file} expands to all selected files in one launch, while a placeholder embedded in an argument launches once per file.

On macOS, apps chosen from the Open with list use the system's open -a handling. A custom command line runs the selected executable path directly; selecting a .app bundle may require its inner executable.

title: fman++ command in PATH
summary: Run fman++ from a Windows terminal by adding its folder to your user PATH.
html:
On Windows, run Toggle command in PATH in the command palette to add or remove the current app's bin folder from your user PATH. After adding it, open a new terminal before typing fman.

The Windows installer adds fman to PATH automatically. If you remove it with the command, later installer updates keep it removed. Uninstalling fman++ removes its PATH entry.

Portable copies can also add their folder to PATH. Turn the command off before moving or deleting a portable folder because the PATH entry points to that location. This command is available only on Windows; Linux packages already install /usr/bin/fman.

title: Portable fman++ for Windows
summary: Run fman++ from an extracted folder or USB drive with its profile stored beside the program.
html:
The portable Windows release is a zip you can extract and run without installing fman++. It keeps settings, plugins and other profile data in a Data folder beside fman.exe.

Start a portable copy

Download fmanPortable.zip from the fman++ GitHub Releases page, extract it to a writable folder such as a USB drive, then open the extracted folder and run fman.exe. fman++ creates the Data folder when needed.

Keep the included portable.txt beside fman.exe to use the local Data profile. Delete the marker to use the usual Windows profile in %APPDATA%\\fman instead; this does not delete the existing Data folder. FMAN_DATA_DIRECTORY, when set by a launcher, takes precedence over both locations.

The portable folder must allow fman++ to create and remove files. If it is read-only or in a protected location such as C:\\Program Files, move or extract it somewhere writable before starting the app.

Updates and multiple copies

Automatic updates are unavailable in portable copies. Check for updates downloads the new fmanPortable.zip; after you confirm, fman++ closes, replaces the program files, keeps the Data folder and files stored beside the program, and starts the updated copy. Leave the folder in place until the update finishes. Installed copies continue to use the installer update flow.

A portable copy and an installed copy can run at the same time with separate profiles. Most profile data moves with the portable folder, but some plugins store absolute paths that do not follow the folder if its drive letter changes. Update those plugin paths after moving the copy.

Portable copies can add themselves to the Windows PATH. before moving or deleting a folder that has been added.

title: Syncing settings between computers
summary: Keep your keyboard shortcuts and command palette names in sync through your fman++ account.
html:
Sign in to the same fman++ account on each computer to sync your custom keyboard shortcuts, command names and search keywords. Settings are kept separately for Windows, Mac and Linux.

the app syncs your own copies of Key Bindings (<OS>).json, Viewer Key Bindings (<OS>).json, Command Titles (<OS>).json and Command Keywords (<OS>).json. Built-in defaults are not uploaded. An absent user file counts as empty; the files stay on each computer, with a separate sync record in Local/Settings Sync.json under the app's data folder.

the app checks for changes after startup and sign-in, and when you run Sync settings from the command palette. Edits made in the app's shortcut or command palette editors are sent right away. If you edit a settings file by hand, the app notices at the next startup or when you run Sync settings.

Choose which copy to keep

If both your computer and your account changed the same setting since the last sync, choose Keep this computer's, Use the account's or Combine both. Combining keeps this computer's value when both copies define the same shortcut or command, and adds entries found only in the account copy. The choice applies to one settings file at a time. Press Escape to leave both copies unchanged; the app asks again at the next sync.

On a computer's first sync, the app asks when the local file and account copy differ. If they match or one side is empty, it can sync without asking. When signed out or offline, local shortcuts and palette edits continue to work. If a sync cannot reach the API, run Sync settings again after reconnecting.

title: Syncing plugins between computers
summary: Keep a shared list of third-party plugins and choose which versions to install on each computer.
html:
Sign in to a fman++ account to keep one list of third-party plugins across your computers. Plugin sync is separate from syncing keyboard shortcuts and command palette names; see Syncing settings between computers.

Run Sign in from the command palette and finish signing in through your browser. Run Sign out to remove the account from this computer; signing out does not delete the shared plugin list.

After a successful Install plugin, the app adds or replaces that plugin in the shared list. Remove plugin removes it. Plugins installed by hand without source information are not uploaded.

Sync the list

the app runs Sync plugins once after startup when the first pane is ready. You can also run it from the command palette. If no account is signed in, startup sync does nothing; a manual sync reports that you are signed out.

  • Plugins in your account list but not installed here appear in a checklist. Entries saved on this operating system start checked; entries saved on another operating system start unchecked and show that system. Selected plugins install at the saved version, not the latest one.
  • Plugins previously shared from this computer but removed from the account list are offered for removal. the app deletes a local copy only after you confirm. If you decline, it stays pending for a later sync.
  • Installed plugins with recognized source information that are missing from the account list are uploaded. Plugins installed by hand without source information are skipped.
  • A plugin removed on this computer while offline is removed from the account list at the next successful sync.

When you skip or leave a plugin unchecked, the app remembers that choice for that version. It is offered again if its saved version changes. A network or account service error appears in the status bar; the next sync compares the current local and remote state again.

The per-computer sync record is stored in Local/Plugin Sync.json under the app's data directory. It is not part of the shared plugin list.

title: Scroll margin
summary: Keep a chosen number of rows visible above and below the keyboard cursor.
html:
The scroll margin keeps rows visible above and below the keyboard cursor, giving you more context while moving through or selecting files. Near the first or last file, the margin shrinks so the cursor can reach the end. Mouse clicks do not move the list.

Set scroll_margin in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json:

{
  "scroll_margin": 3
}

The default is 0, which turns the margin off. Larger values keep the cursor nearer the middle of the visible list. Invalid values count as 0. Restart fman++ after changing this setting.

title: System tray
summary: Keep fman++ available in the Windows notification area while its window is hidden.
html:
On Windows, fman++ can stay running in the notification area (system tray) while its window is hidden. Find the tray commands in the command palette with Ctrl+Shift+P. Closing the window still quits fman++; minimizing and hiding it are separate actions.

Command What it does
Minimize to system tray Hides fman++ and shows its tray icon. Select the icon to restore the window.
Toggle minimize to tray Makes the window's minimize button hide fman++ in the tray. The tray icon stays visible while this is on.
Minimize to taskbar Minimizes the window as usual, leaving it on the taskbar.
Toggle start with Windows In an installed build, starts fman++ hidden in the tray when you sign in.
Toggle Explorer replacement In an installed build, opens folders, drives, Win+E and This PC in fman++. See Explorer replacement.

The tray icon menu has Show and Quit. Quit uses the app's normal exit path and saves the session. When minimize-to-tray is off, the icon appears only while the window is hidden; when it is on, the icon stays visible while fman++ runs.

Start with Windows and hotkeys

In an installed build, Toggle start with Windows starts fman++ hidden in the tray when you sign in. The start_with_windows setting defaults to false.

You can set a Windows-wide key combination with global_hotkey in Local/Settings.json in the app's data directory. For example, add "global_hotkey": "Ctrl+Alt+F". The key is not reserved until you set one. Supported modifiers are Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Win; the final key can be a letter, digit, function key F1–F24, Backspace, Tab, Enter, Escape, Space, PageUp, PageDown, End, Home, an arrow key, Insert or Delete. If another program already uses the combination, fman++ reports that and continues without it. Restart after editing the setting.

The --tray argument starts fman++ hidden in the tray. If another fman++ instance is already running, the launch is forwarded to it without opening a second window. Tray, hotkey and sign-in startup features are Windows-only; start-with-Windows is unavailable in portable and development builds.

You can set a Windows-wide key combination with global_hotkey in Local/Settings.json in the app's data directory. For example, add "global_hotkey": "Ctrl+Alt+F". The key is not reserved until you set one. Supported modifiers are Ctrl, Alt, Shift and Win; the final key can be a letter, digit, function key F1–F24, Backspace, Tab, Enter, Escape, Space, PageUp, PageDown, End, Home, an arrow key, Insert or Delete. If another program already uses the combination, fman++ reports that and continues without it. Restart after editing the setting. The --tray argument starts fman++ hidden in the tray. If another fman++ instance is already running, the launch is forwarded to it without opening a second window. Tray, hotkey and sign-in startup features are Windows-only; start-with-Windows is unavailable in portable and development builds.

title: Windows virtual files
summary: Copy attachments and other files offered by Windows apps even when they are not saved on disk yet.
html:
Some Windows apps offer files without creating them on disk first. For example, Outlook can offer attachments or whole emails. Copy or paste an offered item into the active fman++ pane; emails are saved as .msg files.

fman++ uses its regular copy operation for the transfer, so its confirmations, overwrite prompts, progress, Undo and file-system behavior still apply. Temporary batches older than one day are cleaned up before a new batch is created; younger batches may still be in use by an active copy.

If fman++ cannot set up support for native drag-and-drop, drops keep their previous behavior. Pasting from the clipboard still works. Dragging files from fman++ into an Outlook message is a separate action and is not changed by virtual-file support.

title: Scripting API
summary: Let local scripts read pane state and run commands through fman++ over a protected local API.
html:
The scripting API lets local scripts read fman++ pane state and run commands. It is disabled by default. Run Toggle scripting API from the command palette to start or stop it; the command takes effect immediately. When it starts, the status bar shows the URL and token file path. If enabled in settings, it starts after plugins load.

Connect safely

By default, the API listens only on this computer at http://127.0.0.1:47447. Every request needs a bearer token. fman++ creates the token in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/ScriptingApiToken.txt the first time the API starts and reuses it later. Treat this file as a secret: the token grants access to commands allowed by your settings.

HTTP traffic is unencrypted. Keep the default local-only connection unless you need access from your network. If you enable network access with allowed_hosts, only allow trusted addresses and keep the token private. Anyone who can connect from an allowed address and obtain the token can use the commands permitted by your access settings. A command allowlist limits command names, but plugins can change a command after that check; use command_access: "all" only when you trust every program that can reach the server and has the token.

Requests use UTF-8 JSON. Browser requests that include an Origin header are rejected, request bodies are limited to 1 MB, and errors return a JSON object with an error message.

Read state and run commands

Method and path Purpose
GET /v1/state Read active pane and pane paths, cursor and selection.
GET /v1/commands List pane and application commands and the commands allowed by settings.
POST /v1/command Run an allowed command, with optional arguments and pane.

Panes are listed active-first, so the active pane has index 0. Its path, cursor and selected items are application URLs; the cursor is null when no file is under it. A command defaults to the active pane and empty arguments. Application commands ignore the pane value. The response arrives when the command returns; a copy or move may continue in the background.

For example, a command request can contain {"name":"open_directory","args":{"url":"file://C:/Windows"}}. Each request must include the bearer token in its Authorization header. Use the token from the file path shown in the status bar; do not share it.

Optional desktop automation

Automation routes are available only when scripting_api.automation is true; that setting defaults to false. The routes share the bearer token and network restrictions. They can post key and mouse events inside fman++ but cannot control native operating-system dialogs or global hotkeys. They can read a screenshot, the active dialog and files in a pane. For a visible progress dialog, GET /v1/dialog reports its label and current and maximum progress. Drags that start on a file-list viewport are rejected to prevent starting a file drag-and-drop operation. Automation routes return 403 while automation is disabled.

GET /v1/viewer?pane=0 reports the viewer open in the active pane (pane indexes are active-first). For the video viewer, it also reports whether playback has loaded or is paused, plus the playback position and duration in seconds; position and duration are null until playback loads. When no viewer is open, viewer is null. This route is available only when desktop automation is enabled.

Settings

Settings are in %APPDATA%/fman/Local/Settings.json:

"scripting_api": {
  "enabled": false,
  "automation": false,
  "port": 47447,
  "allowed_hosts": [],
  "command_access": "allowlist",
  "allowed_commands": ["…defaults…"]
}
  • enabled defaults to false. The palette command changes it immediately. Other setting changes apply the next time the API starts.
  • port defaults to 47447 and must be between 1 and 65535.
  • allowed_hosts defaults to an empty list. With no entries the server binds to 127.0.0.1; entries allow matching IP addresses or CIDR networks.
  • command_access defaults to "allowlist". Set it to "all" to allow every command.
  • If you provide allowed_commands, it replaces the defaults. The default list includes navigation, selection, pane switching, reload, sorting and path-copy commands. It excludes destructive and externally launching commands, and excludes Toggle scripting API itself.

title: Drive space
summary: See total capacity and free space for local Windows drives and control how often the list refreshes.
html:
The Windows drives list (drives://) shows each local drive's total capacity and free space in the Size and Free columns. Network drives and drives whose capacity cannot be read are left blank. Values use binary units, including TB.

The list refreshes every 10 seconds while it is open. To change the interval, add this key to Core Settings.json:

{
  "drive_space_refresh_seconds": 30
}

The setting takes effect next time you navigate. Set it to 0 to turn off automatic refresh; press F5 to update the list by hand.

title: Folder refresh
summary: Refresh open local, network and FTP folders automatically to show changes made elsewhere.
html:
Periodic refresh re-reads open folders so changes made by other programs appear without leaving the folder. It runs only while fman++ is the active window. Switching back to fman++ already refreshes both panes.

Use the command palette to toggle refresh separately for local, network and FTP folders:

  • Toggle local folder refresh
  • Toggle network folder refresh
  • Toggle FTP folder refresh

Each category is off by default and has its own interval, initially five seconds. The toggles take effect immediately. Edit Core Settings.json to change these settings:

Setting Default Purpose
refresh_local_folders false Enable refresh for local folders
local_folder_refresh_seconds 5 Local folder interval in seconds
refresh_network_folders false Enable refresh for network folders
network_folder_refresh_seconds 5 Network folder interval in seconds
refresh_ftp_folders false Enable refresh for FTP, FTPS and SFTP folders
ftp_folder_refresh_seconds 5 FTP folder interval in seconds

Hand-edited interval changes take effect the next time you change folders. FTP providers show their usual “Loading…” and “Ready.” messages on each refresh.

title: Add and remove panes
summary: Add file lists to the window or remove the active pane while keeping at least one.
html:
Run Add pane in the command palette to add a file list at the right. It opens in the active pane's folder and receives focus. Run Remove pane to close the active pane; focus moves to the next one, wrapping to the first when needed.

There is always at least one pane, and the pane count is restored when fman++ starts again. Add pane is hidden when no pane is hidden; Remove pane is shown only when more than one pane exists and no pane is hidden. While a pane is hidden with Show only active pane, both commands stay hidden until Show all panes restores the layout.

Neither command has a default key binding, but you can bind either in Key Bindings.json. With one pane, Copy and Move still work; their destination prompt starts at the current folder, which you can edit. Open in left pane and Open in right pane are hidden. Alt+F2 shows volumes in the only pane, and Tab has no other visible pane to focus.

title: Pane sizes
summary: Set equal or custom widths for the file panes and adjust the active pane in small steps.
html:
Run Set pane sizes from the command palette. Choose Equal or set the active pane to 25%, 33%, 67% or 75%; the remaining width is shared evenly by the other panes. You can also run Widen active pane or Narrow active pane to change the active pane by five percentage points. Each command accepts a step argument for a different amount, and these commands do not make a pane narrower than 10%.

You can bind the commands to keys in Key Bindings.json. For example:

{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+7"], "command": "set_pane_sizes", "args": {"sizes": [75, 25]} }
{ "keys": ["Ctrl+Alt+Right"], "command": "widen_active_pane", "args": {"step": 10} }

set_pane_sizes without a sizes argument opens the preset picker. A supplied list sets relative widths directly and must contain one positive number per pane. The commands are hidden when there is only one pane or any pane is hidden. Pane widths are saved with the window state and restored at startup.

title: Edit link target
summary: Change where a symbolic link, directory junction or Windows shortcut points.
html:
Put the cursor on a supported link and choose Edit link target from the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) or the Windows file context menu. The current destination is selected in the input box. Enter a new path and press Enter. Cancel, leave it blank or keep the current destination to make no change.

Command name Palette label Keywords Default key binding
edit_link_target Edit link target symlink, junction, shortcut, lnk, link target, retarget, change link, mklink none

Symbolic links can point to files or folders, and relative targets stay relative to the link's folder. Directory junctions and .lnk shortcuts use an absolute target path. Shortcut arguments, icon and working directory are preserved. This command is for local links; Windows shortcuts are Windows-only, and symbolic links depend on operating-system permissions. Creating symbolic links on Windows may require Developer Mode or an administrator account.

If the new target does not exist, fman++ asks whether to point the link there anyway. Choose Yes to continue or No to keep the current destination. If Windows refuses the change, fman++ reports the error and keeps the existing link.

title: File-age shading
summary: Shade local file rows according to their modified date, with options for the scale and style.
html:
File-age shading changes how file rows look according to their modified date. It is off by default. Run Toggle file age shading in the command palette to turn it on or off; fman++ briefly reports the new state. The setting applies in both panes and remains in effect when you change folders.

Only local files are shaded. Other file systems, missing timestamps and unreadable dates are left unchanged. Future modified dates count as age zero. Selected rows and the cursor row keep their normal appearance.

The options live in Core Settings.json:

Setting Default Effect
file_age_shading false Enables the built-in file-age shading. The command palette toggle changes it while fman++ is running.
file_age_scale "log" "log" fades smoothly; "steps" uses four age levels: under one day, under seven days, under thirty days, and thirty days or older.
file_age_style "transparency" "transparency" fades the row, "tint" blends its text with the theme's pane_new_fg color, and "bold" bolds files modified within the last day.
file_age_full_days 365 Positive number of days at which the logarithmic scale reaches its maximum. Older files are fully shaded.

Invalid values fall back to defaults. Transparency bottoms out at 40% opacity. In the stepped scale, the levels are 0 below one day, 1/3 below seven days, 2/3 below thirty days and 1 from thirty days onward. file_age_full_days affects the logarithmic scale.

title: Toggle hidden files
summary: Show dotfiles and Windows hidden files, or change their faded appearance.
html:
Use Toggle hidden files (Ctrl+.) to show or hide dotfiles and files that Windows marks as hidden. Shown hidden entries have gray icons and paler names; hidden folders stay brighter than hidden files. Selection keeps its usual color, and you can still select, rename and drag these entries.

Change the faded look

Set "dim_hidden_files": false in Core Settings.json to show hidden entries with their normal text and icons. The setting defaults to true. It takes effect the next time you toggle hidden files, reload Core or restart fman++.

Set or remove the Windows hidden attribute

On Windows, use Set hidden attribute or Remove hidden attribute in the command palette. The command acts on selected files or, if none are selected, the file under the cursor. It only changes the Windows hidden attribute; it does not move, rename or delete files. Refresh open panes to see the change. An alert names files fman++ could not change, such as files in protected folders where it cannot request administrator rights.

title: Remember last visited item
summary: Return to a folder with the item you last had under the cursor already selected.
html:
When you return to a location, fman++ selects the file or subfolder you last had under the cursor there. It remembers each level of a visited path, so after visiting a deep folder, its parent selects the next folder on that path. The selection is saved across restarts and works with local folders, archives, FTP/SFTP and plugin locations.

This feature is on by default. Set remember_last_visited in Core Settings.json to false, or run Toggle remember last visited in the command palette to switch it while fman++ is open. When off, existing history remains, but no new visits are recorded or selected. Run Clear last visited history to remove the saved history.

Incognito mode does not record new visits, but it can still select an item remembered earlier. History is stored in Last Visited.json next to Visited Paths.json and keeps up to 1,000 locations; oldest entries are dropped first when the limit is exceeded. For remote URLs that include a password, fman++ removes the password before saving or looking up the location.

html:

When several files are selected, fman++ starts each separately, so Windows may show a prompt for each file. Folders cannot be run this way.

You can bind the command in Key Bindings.json, for example:

Canceling the Windows prompt leaves fman++ open without an error. Windows decides whether a file type supports this action; if it cannot run the file, fman++ shows the error from Windows.

title: Undo file operations
summary: Reverse the latest supported file operation with Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z.
html:
Use Undo to reverse the most recent supported file operation. History lasts only while fman++ is open and is cleared when it exits. Each press undoes one operation, starting with the latest.

Press Ctrl+Z on Windows or Linux, or Cmd+Z on macOS. You can also find Undo in the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P).

Undo supports moving files to the trash, moving files between folders, renaming files and copying files. Undoing a copy asks before moving its copies to the trash. If another file occupies an original location, Undo skips that item and reports failures.

Restoring items from the trash is supported on Windows. On macOS and Linux, Undo reports that trash restoration is unsupported; other supported operations can still be undone. If there is no operation to undo, fman++ says “Nothing to undo.” Undo is not recorded as a new operation. Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z in the in-pane text editor still undoes text edits.

title: Compact view
summary: Show file names in several columns without column headers, like Total Commander's Brief view.
html:
Compact view shows only file names in several columns, like Total Commander's Brief view. Each pane has its own mode, and fman++ restores it when it reopens the session.

To switch the active pane, run Toggle compact view in the command palette. There is no default keyboard shortcut, but you can assign one in the key bindings settings.

Names fill each column from top to bottom, then continue in the next column. Columns use the width of the longest name, up to the pane width. Longer names end in an ellipsis; hover over one to see its full name. File icons remain visible.

Use the usual sort commands and key bindings. Compact view has no column header, so choose a sort in the command palette or use its key binding.
