title: File coloring
summary: Color file names by extension and tune the rules for your files.
html:
File coloring gives file names a color based on their extension. It is off by default. Run Toggle file coloring from the command palette to turn it on or off in both panes.

Settings

The file_coloring setting in Core Settings.json enables the built-in rules. Use Toggle file coloring to change it while fman++ is running. The setting defaults to false.

Use file_color_rules to customize which names get which colors. Rules are checked in order, and the first matching rule wins:

{
  "file_coloring": true,
  "file_color_rules": [
    {"patterns": ["*.jpg", "*.png", "*.svg"], "color": "file_image_fg"},
    {"patterns": ["*.zip", "*.7z", "*.rar"], "color": "#fd971f"},
    {"patterns": ["*.exe", "*.bat", "*.ps1"], "color": "pane_new_fg"}
  ]
}

Patterns match file names without regard to case and support shell-style wildcards such as *.png. A color can be a hex value or a color name from the active theme. The default rules cover common image, archive, audio and video, and program extensions, using the file_image_fg, file_archive_fg, file_media_fg and file_program_fg theme colors. Invalid settings fall back to the defaults, and malformed rules are ignored.

How file colors appear

File colors replace the usual text color. Hidden files stay faded, and file-age shading remains layered over the color. Selected files and the row under the cursor keep their usual colors. You can customize the four file-color theme colors in your theme.

title: Error reports
summary: Choose whether fman++ sends unexpected errors, and see what a report contains.
html:
Released builds of fman++ can send unexpected errors to help the maintainers find and fix crashes. Automatic reporting starts only after you consent. Debug and development builds never send reports.

What a report contains

A report includes the error kind, platform, fman++ version, exception type, message and stack trace. The operating system version and third-party plugin folder name are included when available.

Before delivery, fman++ removes email addresses, bearer tokens, JWT-shaped values, recognized token formats, and values following names such as password, token, secret and key. Messages are limited to 2,000 characters and stack traces to 32,000 characters. The service validates, redacts and limits reports again. Reports do not include request headers, query strings, request bodies or an IP address stored with the report.

Choose whether to send reports

The first time you start fman++, it shows the tutorial instead of the consent question. On a later start, the question appears if either your error-reporting or usage-statistics choice has not been saved. Choose one of these options:

  • Accept all to enable both error reports and usage statistics.
  • Only error reports to enable error reports and leave usage statistics off.
  • Only usage statistics to enable usage statistics and leave error reports off.
  • No thanks to turn both off.

Closing the question also turns both off. You can change the error-reporting setting at any time by running Toggle error reports from the command palette. When automatic reporting is off, an error dialog offers Send report for that individual error. Sending one report does not turn on automatic reporting.

Offline reports and failed deliveries are dropped. They are not saved for later. See Usage metrics for details about the separate usage statistics choice.

title: Usage statistics
summary: See what usage statistics include and choose whether fman++ sends them.
html:
Frozen releases of fman++ can send anonymous usage events to help improve the app. Sending is off until you choose Accept all or Only usage statistics in the consent question. Development builds never send usage statistics.

What is sent

Each batch includes a random installation ID, the platform, the fman++ version, and events with their occurrence time and properties. Events describe app starts, commands, file interactions, context-menu use, tutorial progress and shortcut handling. Properties may include command names, the shortcut pressed, the tutorial step, how a context menu was opened, and text entered in the shortcut dialog's feedback field.

Events have no dedicated fields for file or folder paths, names, contents or account credentials. The feedback field is sent as text, though, so do not enter personal or sensitive information there. The installation ID is generated on your device; fman++ does not create an account for usage statistics, and event batches have no dedicated name or email field.

Choose whether to send statistics

The shared consent question offers Accept all, Only error reports, Only usage statistics and No thanks. Closing it turns both error reporting and usage statistics off. See Error reports for more about the other choice.

Run Toggle usage statistics from the command palette to change the setting while fman++ is open. Restart fman++ for the change to take effect.

If delivery fails, including while you are offline, that batch is dropped. It is not retried or saved for later, and a delivery failure does not prevent you from closing or using the app.
